counterfactual_missing_items: Histopathologic confirmation of non-caseating granulomas with lobular inflammation
Microbiologic or histochemical support for tuberculosis or bacterial mastitis
Evidence specifically localizing inflammation to ductal or periductal tissue
decisive_items: tender swelling in the outer half of the right breast with overlying warmth, erythema, and nipple retraction
a skin fistula developed with pus extruding and an “orange peel” appearance of the overlying skin
Breast MRI revealed multiple oval and rounded lesions with irregular thick walls throughout the gland, extending to the skin, with peripheral enhancement
response.rationale: C1 wins by combining R5’s specific diagnosis and the documented right-sided location, which R5 omits. R2 is a less specific expression of the same broad entity, while R1 uses only non-specific physical findings and cannot account for the MRI and negative-infectious-workup context.

rejected.why: Less specific umbrella; R5 and C1 provide the more precise lobular and idiopathic characterization supported by the same raw spans.
Its chosen findings are compatible but too non-specific; the multifocal thick-walled MRI pattern and normality of the infectious work-up favor the granulomatous-lobular differential.
